description: Every Docker and Swarm concept the inventory can carry, with each systemd target that can express it, the directives involved, and an honest fidelity rating. plan-map.ts selects the rows an estate needs and computes the systemd version each row requires from the directive catalogue; the harness tests check every directive and tool named here against that catalogue.

fidelity_levels.exact: the same behaviour, expressed with systemd directives
fidelity_levels.equivalent: the same outcome by different means; the difference is documented
fidelity_levels.partial: a documented loss; the row produces a MIGRATION-NOTES entry
fidelity_levels.manual: a runbook step that no renderer performs

targets.service: a plain unit whose root is the image's mount stack (RootMStack=) or a DDI (RootImage=)
targets.nspawn: a machine run by systemd-nspawn@.service with a .nspawn file
targets.vmspawn: a virtual machine run by systemd-vmspawn@.service from a bootable DDI
targets.portable: a portable service image attached with portablectl
targets.capsule: a per-stack user manager started by capsule@.service
targets.sysext: a system extension image merged into /usr/
targets.confext: a configuration extension image merged into /etc/
targets.networkd: .netdev, .network, .link, and .dnssd files for systemd-networkd and systemd-resolved
targets.quadlet: a Podman Quadlet unit, rendered by podman-quadlet
targets.runbook: an operator step in the migration plan

needs: kernel 6.13 for a writable layer (overlayfs FSCONFIG_SET_FD)
targets.how: importctl pull-oci --class=machine REF NAME writes NAME.mstack/ with one layer@N per image layer; the digest is recorded in the unit's [X-Migration] section; several versions live side by side as NAME.raw.v/ (systemd.v).
systemd-nspawn --mstack=NAME.mstack boots or runs the merged tree; an unpacked OCI bundle is accepted with --oci-bundle=.
Fallback for hosts before version 260 or kernels before 6.13: the merged tree is packed into a DDI by systemd-repart --make-ddi and mounted with RootImage=.

concepts.concept: Image entrypoint, command, environment, working directory, user
concepts.note: importctl pull-oci does not preserve the OCI image configuration; the planner reads it from the inventory (docker service inspect merges it) and the renderer synthesises the directives.

targets.how: entrypoint plus args become ExecStart=; a numeric user becomes User= and Group=, an absent one becomes DynamicUser=yes.
Boot=no with Parameters= runs the entrypoint as the container's init; Boot=yes is for images that ship an init system.
The process runs in the image's tree with the host kernel and systemd's sandboxing instead of a container runtime; PrivateUsers=self gives it an unprivileged user namespace.
ProcessTwo=yes keeps a stub init as PID 1 the way docker run --init does; PrivateUsers=pick maps the machine to an unprivileged range.
Podman runs the container and Quadlet generates the unit; see podman-quadlet.

concepts.concept: Service booting a full OS image

targets.how: systemd-nspawn@NAME.service with Boot=yes; the machine joins machines.target and machinectl manages it.

concepts.concept: Replicas and mode: global, replicated job, global job

targets.how: A template NAME@.service with one instance per replica per host, all in stack-<name>.slice; mode global becomes one instance on every eligible host. Swarm scheduling across the cluster becomes a host assignment in the plan. A replicated job or global job becomes Type=oneshot with RemainAfterExit=no and no Restart=; Swarm records no schedule, so the plan asks for one and an OnCalendar expression renders a <service>.timer with Persistent=yes that the stack target wants in the service place.
<stack>.target wants every unit of the stack; stack-<name>.slice groups their cgroups; the unit's [X-Migration] section records Stack=.

The host map assigns each service to hosts; ConditionHost= guards a unit against being started elsewhere; node labels are recorded in /etc/machine-info as DEPLOYMENT= and LOCATION=. A spread preference groups the eligible hosts by its descriptor and hands instances to the groups round-robin, and max_replicas_per_node caps the instances one host may carry, with the replicas it leaves unplaced noted on the placement decision.

condition any becomes Restart=always, on-failure becomes Restart=on-failure, none becomes Restart=no; delay becomes RestartSec=, keeping sub-second precision; max_attempts becomes StartLimitBurst= and window becomes StartLimitIntervalSec=. Swarm never gives up when max_attempts is 0 or absent, so the unit gets StartLimitIntervalSec=0 rather than the manager default, and a budget with no window gets infinity, which counts over any interval. The limit counts every start, including the restart the health unit performs.

concepts.concept: Stop grace period and stop signal

targets.how: KillMode=mixed sends the signal to the main process first, as Docker does, then SIGKILL to the rest after TimeoutStopSec=.
KillSignal= in the .nspawn file; the timeout stays on the systemd-nspawn@ unit.

NAME-health.timer runs NAME-health.service at the interval with the timeout; after the retries its OnFailure= restarts NAME.service. An application that speaks sd_notify uses WatchdogSec= instead, and start_period becomes TimeoutStartSec= with Type=notify.
NotifyReady=yes waits for the payload's READY=1 before the machine counts as started.

The runbook restarts instances in batches of the configured parallelism with the configured delay; images under NAME.raw.v/ let a rollback pick the previous version by name; RefreshOnReload= reloads credentials without a restart.
limits.nano_cpus becomes CPUQuota=, limits.memory_bytes MemoryMax=, reservations.memory_bytes MemoryLow=, limits.pids TasksMax=; the same properties apply to nspawn through --property=.
cap_add and cap_drop become CapabilityBoundingSet= and AmbientCapabilities=; privileged: true is never rendered, it becomes a note asking which capabilities the workload uses.
The same sets in the .nspawn file; nspawn's default capability set is close to Docker's.

Each ulimit becomes the matching Limit*= directive; a sysctl becomes a sysctl.d/ fragment on the host (a note, since it changes the host) or is applied inside an nspawn machine's own namespace where the key allows.
DevicePolicy=closed with one DeviceAllow= per device; nspawn additionally binds the node with Bind=.
stdout and stderr go to the journal with the stack and service as extra fields; json-file size limits become journald's own retention.
LinkJournal=try-guest makes the machine's journal readable from the host with journalctl -M.

Each secret becomes a credential encrypted with systemd-creds and loaded with LoadCredentialEncrypted=name:/etc/credstore.encrypted/name; the process reads it under $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY; values are never rendered, the import script asks the operator for them.
--load-credential= passes the credential into the machine, where it appears under /run/host/credentials/.
The payload is written to /etc/<stack>/<name> with the recorded ownership and mode and bound read-only at the target path.
All of a stack's configs become one configuration extension image whose extension-release carries ID=_any, merged into /etc/ by systemd-confext.
Plain values become Environment=; redacted values become credentials (see secrets) and a note; a long environment goes to /etc/<stack>/<service>.env with mode 0600.
The service binds the port itself; SocketBindAllow= and SocketBindDeny=any enforce the declared set; an application that accepts an inherited socket gets a .socket unit instead and starts on demand.
Port=tcp:80:8080 installs a DNAT rule from the host to the machine's address on the zone or veth link.

concepts.concept: Published ports through the routing mesh

targets.how: No routing mesh exists on a systemd host. The plan chooses per port: host mode on every host that runs the service, nspawn Port= on one host, or a front proxy or load balancer that the plan names. Until chosen, the renderer publishes in host mode and writes a note.

concepts.concept: Overlay network confined to one host

targets.how: A bridge per network: nspawn machines join it with Zone=<net> (the shipped 80-container-vz.network configures vz-* bridges, and the rendered drop-in replaces its 0.0.0.0/24 with the Swarm IPAM subnet); services on the host reach it through the bridge address; fixed addresses become [DHCPServerStaticLease] entries.

A vxlan netdev per network bridged into the zone bridge on each host; an encrypted overlay puts the vxlan on a wireguard link between the hosts, a plain one rides the underlay. Keys are credentials, never rendered.

Machines get MACVLAN= or IPVLAN= on the parent link; inside the machine the new 80-container-mv.network and 80-container-iv.network configure mv-* and iv-* links the way host0 is configured today; a service on the host gets a macvlan netdev in bridge mode.
Private=no shares the host namespace; a plain service is in the host namespace already.

Names resolve through the zone bridge's DHCP leases (the lease domain), mDNS and LLMNR on the link, and .dnssd files for services that should be discoverable; the estate's search domain goes to resolved.conf.d/. A Swarm VIP becomes one address per host, which the plan must front.

concepts.concept: Named volumes with the local driver

targets.how: /var/lib/<stack>/<volume>/ is created by a tmpfiles.d d line with the owner the service runs as and bound at the mount target; a DynamicUser= service uses StateDirectory= instead.

concepts.concept: Volumes with a network driver (nfs, cifs)

targets.how: A .mount unit per volume from the driver options (type, o, device), an .automount when idle unmount is wanted, and RequiresMountsFor= on every consumer.
Bind mounts keep their source path and read-only flag; a tmpfs with a size becomes TemporaryFileSystem=/path:size=.
Optional: a repart.d/ definition creates a data partition for /var/lib/<stack> at first boot on a freshly provisioned host.
depends_on becomes After= plus Wants= (Requires= for condition: service_started, and After= the health service for service_healthy); a profile becomes a target.

concepts.concept: Compose init, pid, ipc, read_only, extra_hosts, dns

targets.how: read_only becomes ProtectSystem=strict, pid and ipc isolation become PrivatePIDs= and PrivateIPC=, hostname becomes ProtectHostname=private:<name> in the service own UTS namespace, extra_hosts becomes a bound /etc/hosts, dns becomes per-link DNS= or a bound resolv.conf. init and tty are notes: the service manager reaps orphans the injected init would have reaped, and a service has no pseudo-terminal.
ProcessTwo= for init, ReadOnly= for read_only, ResolvConf= for dns.

The image directory under /var/lib/portables/ carries os-release with PORTABLE_PREFIXES= and the rendered units; the profile is chosen from default, nonetwork, strict, and trusted; shared runtimes ride along as extension images.
Only for images whose payload is a pure /usr/ overlay (ID=_any in extension-release.NAME unless the base is known); anything that writes to /etc/ or /var/ is rejected with a note.
capsule@<stack>.service starts a user manager for the stack; each service is a user unit under /var/lib/capsules/<stack>/.config/systemd/user/ with RootMStack=.
A bootable DDI built by systemd-repart --make-ddi from the merged mount stack plus a kernel, run by systemd-vmspawn@NAME.service; the shipped 80-vm-vt.network configures the host side.
There is no cluster manager; the runbook covers node roles, maintenance with systemctl isolate, and machinectl for the machines on each host.
